header.name: Advanced Sociological Theory
header.description: This course grounds students in sociological theory - both classical and contemporary. Developed as an advanced theory course the readings are at a graduate level. Sociological theory has undergone transitions and shifts and the course will alert students to theoretical themes and debates. Considered as schools of thought, the course will enable students to understand theoretical foundations and conclusions that shape methodological entry points. The course enables students to consider imminent as well as external critiques in order to analyse social changes and political shifts. At the end of the course students will have an in-depth understanding and analysis of major schools of thought in sociology.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can understand and analyse the context of emergence and themes of different schools of thought

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students can explain different theoretical approaches and develop a comparative understanding on contemporary issues.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can develop and generate a theoretical framework for their own research.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can analyse inter-disciplinary connections in the realm of sociological theory and critically evaluate theoretical frameworks
